"The Heart of BeamNG: Soft-Body Physics
​At the core of BeamNG.drive is its proprietary soft-body physics engine, which replaced rigid-body physics traditionally used in video games.
​Nodes and Beams Architecture: Every vehicle is constructed from a vast web of microscopic \"nodes\" (mass points) connected by \"beams\" (spring-like elements with properties like elasticity, strength, and deformation limits).
​Real-Time Stress Calculation: When a car impacts an obstacle, the engine calculates real-time stress across thousands of individual beams. If a beam exceeds its yield strength, it bends permanently; if it exceeds its ultimate strength, it snaps.
​Complex Material Behavior: Materials aren't just uniform metal sheets. The physics model distinguishes between frame rails, thin body panels, glass (which shatters dynamically), rubber tires, and suspension arms, causing realistic buckling, twisting, and crumpling.
​2. Crash Physics @COMMENT_BODY@ Mechanical Simulation
​BeamNG doesn't just look like it's crashing; it simulates the internal mechanical forces causing the crash.
​Full Powertrain Simulation: The engine models internal combustion mechanics down to individual pistons, valves, and turbochargers. Overrevving an engine can float valves or throw a rod; punching a hole in the oil pan causes oil starvation and engine seizure.
​Drivetrain @COMMENT_BODY@ Suspension Dynamics: Driveshafts can twist and snap under high torque, differentials lock or break realistically, and suspension geometry changes dynamically as control arms bend.
​Tire Physics @COMMENT_BODY@ Aerodynamics: Tires experience realistic deflation, sidewall flexing, and temperature/pressure changes. Airflow creates dynamic downforce and drag, meaning a missing door or crumpled hood alters how the car handles mid-flight.
​3. Graphics, Environment, and Fidelity
​Powered by a heavily modified version of the Torque3D engine, BeamNG pairs its heavy-duty physics with impressive visual and environmental fidelity.Feature Details
Lighting @COMMENT_BODY@ PBR Physical-Based Rendering (PBR) materials ensure paint, chrome, rubber, and glass react accurately to dynamic time-of-day lighting and weather.
Environments Massive open-world maps ranging from dense urban cities and tight mountain passes (like East Coast USA or Utah) to rugged off-road trails and stunt arenas.
Particle @COMMENT_BODY@ Surface Effects Dynamic tire smoke, dust plumes, mud accumulation, sparks from metal scraping against asphalt, and realistic water physics.
Sound Design Audio is tightly synchronized with mechanical stress—screeching tires, groaning chassis frames, supercharger whines, and crunching metal change pitch and intensity based on velocity and deformation.4. Gameplay, Modes, and Sandbox Freedom
​While famous for its crash testing sandbox, BeamNG offers robust gameplay systems:
​Free Roam @COMMENT_BODY@ Traffic AI: Spawn anywhere on any map, place traffic cars controlled by intelligent AI, and simulate police pursuits or highway pile-ups.
​Scenarios @COMMENT_BODY@ Time Trials: Precision driving challenges, delivery missions, high-speed jumps, and stunt courses.
​Career Mode: An expanding role-playing mode where players buy vehicles, manage repair costs, take on transport jobs, and build up a garage from scratch.
​Built-in World Editor: A fully functional developer toolset allowing players to alter terrain, spawn objects, edit vehicle files, and create custom tracks directly inside the game. And add realistic character customisation and smooth closing and opening door customisations and realistic windows. And car engine sounds.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
